answer_verification_r5.author_derivation: Original x=1/(2t+1)², y=sqrt(t+2). For finite derivative t>−2,t≠−1/2: dx/dt=−4/(2t+1)³,dy/dt=1/(2sqrt(t+2)), hence dy/dx=−(2t+1)³/(8sqrt(t+2)). Gradient−1 implies (2p+1)³=8sqrt(p+2)>0, so p>−1/2. Take REAL cube root to obtain2p+1=2(p+2)^(1/6), and divide2. Genuine parametric geometry, not an explicit-function item.

answer_verification_r5.author_derivation: For a reduced polynomial division,if a nonzero remainderRhad degree at leastn,its leading term could be cancelled by subtracting a suitable multiple of the divisor. This independently derives the statement in the printed key.

The printed key states the all-values versus particular-value distinction and notes equating constant terms corresponds to x=0.

defects.issue: The more-than column repeats a ≤ caption. Its |x|≥4 example prints x≤−4 or x≥−4 (the diagram correctly marks −4,+4). Bottom notes assert all-real outcomes for b>0 or b≥0, which are false. The opening two-or-more solutions claim also omits zero/one-root modulus equations.
defects.correct_answer: |x|≥4 gives x≤−4 or x≥4. For b<0, |a|>b and |a|≥b hold for all real a. For b=0, > excludes a=0 while ≥ includes all a. For b>0, use two exterior rays. |a|≤b has no solution for b<0 and only a=0 for b=0.
